methodology.rule: A claim may be VERIFIED or EXECUTED only when a resident mechanism and executable evidence reference are both present. Otherwise the record must identify the exact missing mechanism.

claims.claim: BRAINK can compile a service undertaking into named capability requirements and distinguish reusable resident bindings from unresolved requirements.
GitHub-hosted CI currently provides executed qualification evidence for the R18/R19 runtime.
claims.failure_reason: Observed GitHub Actions jobs failed before any workflow step executed with no allocated runner, so source tests were not executed by the hosted CI environment.
claims.missing_mechanism: A functioning CI runner allocation/executor path that actually executes the declared workflow steps.

claims.claim: HR assignment records bind agent identity, roles, sector, capabilities and target authority scope, and authorize rejects mismatched sector/capability/scope.
HR has qualified runtime semantics for supervision, lease, replacement and rehydration across process interruption.
claims.failure_reason: The current HR runtime verifies assignment, revocation and authorization but no inspected HR mechanism proves supervision leases, replacement or rehydration semantics.
claims.missing_mechanism: Durable supervisor/child lease state, expiry/fencing rule, replacement transition and rehydration receipt with deterministic tests.

claims.claim: Runtime/server work accepts the common BRAINK SectorTask envelope and emits content-rooted SectorReceipt state with explicit capability-hole behavior.
The runtime sector has independently verified health, restart and release-qualification execution semantics for hosted workloads.
claims.failure_reason: The R18 sector binding proves federation membership and ABI compatibility, not actual process health/restart behavior.
claims.missing_mechanism: Executable health probe, restart state machine, crash/restart tests and release qualification receipt in the runtime-server repository.

claims.claim: BRAINK has verified artifact addressability, backing lineage, checkpoint and software content-hash capabilities usable by storage genomes.
Storage backing is proven durable across physical multi-host failure and network partitions.
claims.failure_reason: Current evidence supports local/reference backing and lineage semantics, not physical multi-host durability or partition behavior.
claims.missing_mechanism: Distinct-host replicated backing, fault-injection/partition tests, consistency model and durable recovery receipts.

claims.claim: Research/learning/evolution is bound into the common sector federation and can receive shared BRAINK work-module envelopes.
Research outputs are automatically scored for evidence quality, reproducibility and market-feasibility accuracy before promotion.
claims.failure_reason: The inspected federation contract routes work but does not prove a research-quality or reproducibility gate.
claims.missing_mechanism: Research evidence schema, source/provenance score, reproducibility test and independent promotion gate.

claims.claim: BRAINK has a bounded self-coding workgroup path that requires an explicit work-module contract and tests before a generated capability is registered.
Generated functions are independently promoted into production sector runtimes with enforced separation of synthesizer, verifier and promoter.
claims.failure_reason: Bounded synthesis was validated locally, but this R19 audit does not have an executed production promotion transaction spanning independent verifier/promoter identities.
claims.missing_mechanism: End-to-end promotion transaction with independent identities, immutable provenance, rollback reference and production readback receipt.

claims.claim: The mesh/software-nodes repository is explicitly bound to BRAINK R18 for mesh, routing, membership, fencing and transport capability classes.
The current mesh/fencing stack is proven safe and live across physically distinct hosts and WAN partitions.
claims.failure_reason: Existing KEX fencing evidence is local/separate-process or fixed-membership reference evidence; physical distinct-host/WAN execution was not established by this audit.
claims.missing_mechanism: Distinct-host deployment, partition/failover tests, network timing assumptions and readback receipts from each host.

claims.claim: The mining repository is bound to BRAINK R18 with Bitcoin Core, job-dispatch, block-template, SHA256d, submission and receipt capability classes.
The mining service currently proves live mainnet node synchronization through full block construction and submitblock receipt.
claims.failure_reason: The federation binding names required capability classes but is not itself execution evidence for a synchronized node, complete block assembly or accepted submitblock transaction.
claims.missing_mechanism: Live bitcoind sync evidence, getblocktemplate receipt, complete block assembly test and submitblock receipt.

claims.claim: The console/UI repository is bound to BRAINK R18 for operator-console, runtime-projection, observer-projection and admin-UI capability classes.
Every operator UI control is traced to an authorized backend action, state mutation and rollback/readback receipt.
claims.failure_reason: The R18 binding proves federation membership but this audit has not established end-to-end action tracing for every UI control.
claims.missing_mechanism: Control-to-command registry, HR authorization binding, backend receipt and rollback/readback invariant for each actionable control.
